title: Elodie and the Clock
premise: In the final winter of a grinding continental war, Elodie Marchand works as a battlefield nurse in the occupied town of Saint-Aubin, quietly recording in her ledger the names of soldiers the officers' reports omit — the deserters shot at dawn, the civilians caught in crossfire, the boys who died before their paperwork arrived. When the army requisitions the town and orders all documents surrendered, her ledger becomes both contraband and confession. With help from a found family of townsfolk and one conflicted requisition officer who may be the brother of a name in her book, she must smuggle it past three checkpoints to the armistice commission before the ceasefire is signed — or collapses. She reaches the commission as the guns fall silent, trading her invisibility for testimony, and chooses truth over the safety anonymity once offered.
about_author: Emrys Sandoval is the pen name of a former field medic turned archivist who spent a decade cataloguing unclaimed letters from forgotten wars. They write historical fiction about the people history files under 'miscellaneous.'

chapters.title: The Weight of Small Names
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. A night shift in the converted convent hospital introduces her ritual: recording names the officers omit in a hidden ledger. We meet the found family — cook Marguerite, orderly Tomas, wounded private Anselm. Emotional beat: quiet devotion disguised as routine.

chapters.title: Requisition Papers
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Colonel Vasseur announces the army is taking the town; every document, register, and personal paper must be surrendered by week's end. Elodie hides the ledger inside a hymnal. Beat: dread beneath obedience.

chapters.title: What the Hymnal Holds
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Tomas discovers Elodie's secret when he nearly donates the hymnal. Instead of betraying her, he offers to help. Beat: the first brick of found family laid deliberately.

chapters.title: The Officer Who Counts Twice
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Requisition officer Lieutenant Aurel Brenner arrives to inventory the hospital — meticulous, haunted, and carrying a photograph of a brother listed missing. Elodie recognizes the name from her ledger's pages. Beat: dangerous recognition.

chapters.title: Marguerite's Kitchen Table
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. The kitchen becomes a war council: three checkpoints stand between Saint-Aubin and the armistice commission at Verrières. Marguerite proposes hiding the ledger in a coffin bound for burial outside the lines. Beat: resolve hardening into plan.

chapters.title: Anselm's Confession
chapters.summary: Anselm's POV. Recovering enough to walk, Anselm admits he deserted once and was pardoned only because his death was misreported — his real name sits in Elodie's book. He insists on carrying the ledger himself. Beat: guilt transformed into purpose.

chapters.title: First Checkpoint: The Mill Bridge
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Disguised as a grief-stricken widow escorting her cousin's coffin, Elodie passes the mill bridge checkpoint — but Brenner is stationed there and looks too long at her face. Beat: terror threaded with composure.

chapters.title: The Ledger Read Backward
chapters.summary: Brenner's POV. Alone, Brenner recalls auditing casualty reports that never matched his own counts, and begins pulling threads on Vasseur's omissions. He finds his brother's name absent from official records. Beat: loyalty to the army cracking.

chapters.title: A Town That Forgets Itself
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. With papers seized, the townsfolk begin erasing their own histories — burning letters, scraping gravestones. Tomas organizes a silent resistance: memorizing names aloud each evening. Beat: communal defiance.

chapters.title: Second Checkpoint: The Salt Road
chapters.summary: Anselm's POV. Anselm takes the coffin alone through the salt road checkpoint, where a sergeant knew him before his desertion. He talks his way through by confessing to a smaller sin than the true one. Beat: identity as performance and peril.

chapters.title: Vasseur Summons the Nurse
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Vasseur interrogates Elodie about a missing hymnal, revealing he knows more than he says — and that the armistice may collapse, extending the occupation indefinitely. Beat: the clock starts ticking audibly.

chapters.title: Brenner's Bargain
chapters.summary: Brenner's POV. Brenner confronts Elodie privately: he has deduced the ledger exists. He offers silence in exchange for proof of what happened to his brother. Beat: two loyalties negotiating across a table.

chapters.title: The Page That Isn't There
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Searching her memory, Elodie realizes she never recorded how Brenner's brother died — she arrived too late. The truth must come from a dying witness in the ward: old Sergeant Pelay, Vasseur's own man. Beat: truth requiring an enemy's testimony.

chapters.title: Pelay's Last Watch
chapters.summary: Pelay's POV. The dying sergeant dictates his account: Vasseur ordered the retreat that abandoned Brenner's brother's unit, then scrubbed the records. Pelay signs the page. Beat: a soldier reclaiming honor at the end.

chapters.title: Third Checkpoint: The Chapel Gate
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. The final checkpoint guards the road to Verrières. Marguerite volunteers, weaponizing her age and grief as the town's beloved cook, while the others create a diversion — a fire in the requisitioned granary. Beat: sacrifice offered freely.

chapters.title: Fire and Fog
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. The diversion spirals; Tomas is arrested, and Vasseur connects the fire to the missing ledger. He orders the roads sealed until after the signing. Beat: the plan breaking apart.

chapters.title: The Clock in the Convent Tower
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. The convent's broken clock, stopped since the occupation began, is repaired by the townsfolk as a signal — when it strikes again, the armistice is signed. Elodie has hours, not days. Beat: time made audible.

chapters.title: What Brenner Carries
chapters.summary: Brenner's POV. Ordered to seal the chapel gate, Brenner instead walks Elodie through it himself, carrying Pelay's signed page as his passport past his own conscience. Beat: betrayal of an institution for fidelity to truth.

chapters.title: Verrières Before the Ink Dries
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Elodie reaches the armistice commission as delegates argue over final terms. She presents the ledger and Pelay's testimony, demanding the omitted names be read into the record. Beat: the invisible made undeniable.

chapters.title: Vasseur's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Vasseur's POV. Facing inquiry, Vasseur defends his omissions as mercy and arithmetic — fewer names, fewer widows. Elodie answers that a name is not a number. He is relieved of command as the guns begin to quiet. Beat: the antagonist's logic met and refused.

chapters.title: The Clock Strikes
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV, rotating brief passages. In Saint-Aubin, the repaired clock strikes twelve as word arrives: the armistice holds. Tomas is released; Marguerite rings the bell; Anselm stands in the square under his true name. Beat: collective exhale.

chapters.title: A Ledger Left Open
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Months later, Elodie testifies publicly, no longer hiding, and leaves the final pages of a new ledger blank — for names yet to be lived, not lost. Brenner visits with his brother's restored record. Beat: identity chosen, family kept, truth ongoing.
